# solana_transaction/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)#![cfg_attr(feature = "frozen-abi", feature(min_specialization))]
[2](https://docs.rs#2)#![cfg_attr(docsrs, feature(doc_cfg))]
[3](https://docs.rs#3)#![no_std]
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//! Atomically-committed sequences of instructions.
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//!
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! While [`Instruction`]s are the basic unit of computation in Solana, they are
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//! submitted by clients in [`Transaction`]s containing one or more
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//! instructions, and signed by one or more [`Signer`]s. Solana executes the
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//! instructions in a transaction in order, and only commits any changes if all
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//! instructions terminate without producing an error or exception.
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//!
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//! Transactions do not directly contain their instructions but instead include
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! a [`Message`], a precompiled representation of a sequence of instructions.
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//! `Message`'s constructors handle the complex task of reordering the
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//! individual lists of accounts required by each instruction into a single flat
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//! list of deduplicated accounts required by the Solana runtime. The
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//! `Transaction` type has constructors that build the `Message` so that clients
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//! don't need to interact with them directly.
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//!
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//! Prior to submission to the network, transactions must be signed by one or
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//! more keypairs, and this signing is typically performed by an abstract
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//! [`Signer`], which may be a [`Keypair`] but may also be other types of
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//! signers including remote wallets, such as Ledger devices, as represented by
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//! the [`RemoteKeypair`] type in the [`solana-remote-wallet`] crate.
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//!
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//! [`Signer`]: https://docs.rs/solana-signer/latest/solana_signer/trait.Signer.html
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//! [`Keypair`]: https://docs.rs/solana-keypair/latest/solana_keypair/struct.Keypair.html
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//! [`solana-remote-wallet`]: https://docs.rs/solana-remote-wallet/latest/
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//! [`RemoteKeypair`]: https://docs.rs/solana-remote-wallet/latest/solana_remote_wallet/remote_keypair/struct.RemoteKeypair.html
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//!
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//! Every transaction must be signed by a fee-paying account, the account from
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//! which the cost of executing the transaction is withdrawn. Other required
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//! signatures are determined by the requirements of the programs being executed
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//! by each instruction, and are conventionally specified by that program's
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//! documentation.
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//!
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//! When signing a transaction, a recent blockhash must be provided (which can
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//! be retrieved with [`RpcClient::get_latest_blockhash`]). This allows
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//! validators to drop old but unexecuted transactions; and to distinguish
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//! between accidentally duplicated transactions and intentionally duplicated
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//! transactions — any identical transactions will not be executed more
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//! than once, so updating the blockhash between submitting otherwise identical
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//! transactions makes them unique. If a client must sign a transaction long
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//! before submitting it to the network, then it can use the _[durable
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//! transaction nonce]_ mechanism instead of a recent blockhash to ensure unique
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//! transactions.
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//!
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//! [`RpcClient::get_latest_blockhash`]: https://docs.rs/solana-rpc-client/latest/solana_rpc_client/rpc_client/struct.RpcClient.html#method.get_latest_blockhash
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//! [durable transaction nonce]: https://docs.solanalabs.com/implemented-proposals/durable-tx-nonces
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//!
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//! # Examples
[52](https://docs.rs#52)//!
[53](https://docs.rs#53)//! This example uses the [`solana_rpc_client`] and [`anyhow`] crates.
[54](https://docs.rs#54)//!
[55](https://docs.rs#55)//! [`solana_rpc_client`]: https://docs.rs/solana-rpc-client
[56](https://docs.rs#56)//! [`anyhow`]: https://docs.rs/anyhow
[57](https://docs.rs#57)//!
[58](https://docs.rs#58)//! ```
[59](https://docs.rs#59)//! # use solana_example_mocks::{solana_keypair, solana_rpc_client, solana_signer, solana_transaction};
[60](https://docs.rs#60)//! use anyhow::Result;
[61](https://docs.rs#61)//! use borsh::{BorshSerialize, BorshDeserialize};
[62](https://docs.rs#62)//! use solana_instruction::Instruction;
[63](https://docs.rs#63)//! use solana_keypair::Keypair;
[64](https://docs.rs#64)//! use solana_message::Message;
[65](https://docs.rs#65)//! use solana_pubkey::Pubkey;
[66](https://docs.rs#66)//! use solana_rpc_client::rpc_client::RpcClient;
[67](https://docs.rs#67)//! use solana_signer::Signer;
[68](https://docs.rs#68)//! use solana_transaction::Transaction;
[69](https://docs.rs#69)//!
[70](https://docs.rs#70)//! // A custom program instruction. This would typically be defined in
[71](https://docs.rs#71)//! // another crate so it can be shared between the on-chain program and
[72](https://docs.rs#72)//! // the client.
[73](https://docs.rs#73)//! #[derive(BorshSerialize, BorshDeserialize)]
[74](https://docs.rs#74)//! enum BankInstruction {
[75](https://docs.rs#75)//!     Initialize,
[76](https://docs.rs#76)//!     Deposit { lamports: u64 },
[77](https://docs.rs#77)//!     Withdraw { lamports: u64 },
[78](https://docs.rs#78)//! }
[79](https://docs.rs#79)//!
[80](https://docs.rs#80)//! fn send_initialize_tx(
[81](https://docs.rs#81)//!     client: &RpcClient,
[82](https://docs.rs#82)//!     program_id: Pubkey,
[83](https://docs.rs#83)//!     payer: &Keypair
[84](https://docs.rs#84)//! ) -> Result<()> {
[85](https://docs.rs#85)//!
[86](https://docs.rs#86)//!     let bank_instruction = BankInstruction::Initialize;
[87](https://docs.rs#87)//!
[88](https://docs.rs#88)//!     let instruction = Instruction::new_with_borsh(
[89](https://docs.rs#89)//!         program_id,
[90](https://docs.rs#90)//!         &bank_instruction,
[91](https://docs.rs#91)//!         vec![],
[92](https://docs.rs#92)//!     );
[93](https://docs.rs#93)//!
[94](https://docs.rs#94)//!     let blockhash = client.get_latest_blockhash()?;
[95](https://docs.rs#95)//!     let mut tx = Transaction::new_signed_with_payer(
[96](https://docs.rs#96)//!         &[instruction],
[97](https://docs.rs#97)//!         Some(&payer.pubkey()),
[98](https://docs.rs#98)//!         &[payer],
[99](https://docs.rs#99)//!         blockhash,
[100](https://docs.rs#100)//!     );
[101](https://docs.rs#101)//!     client.send_and_confirm_transaction(&tx)?;
[102](https://docs.rs#102)//!
[103](https://docs.rs#103)//!     Ok(())
[104](https://docs.rs#104)//! }
[105](https://docs.rs#105)//! #
[106](https://docs.rs#106)//! # let client = RpcClient::new(String::new());
[107](https://docs.rs#107)//! # let program_id = Pubkey::new_unique();
[108](https://docs.rs#108)//! # let payer = Keypair::new();
[109](https://docs.rs#109)//! # send_initialize_tx(&client, program_id, &payer)?;
[110](https://docs.rs#110)//! #
[111](https://docs.rs#111)//! # Ok::<(), anyhow::Error>(())
[112](https://docs.rs#112)//! ```

[168](https://docs.rs#168)/// An atomically-committed sequence of instructions.
[169](https://docs.rs#169)///
[170](https://docs.rs#170)/// While [`Instruction`]s are the basic unit of computation in Solana,
[171](https://docs.rs#171)/// they are submitted by clients in [`Transaction`]s containing one or
[172](https://docs.rs#172)/// more instructions, and signed by one or more [`Signer`]s.
[173](https://docs.rs#173)///
[174](https://docs.rs#174)/// [`Signer`]: https://docs.rs/solana-signer/latest/solana_signer/trait.Signer.html
[175](https://docs.rs#175)///
[176](https://docs.rs#176)/// See the [module documentation] for more details about transactions.
[177](https://docs.rs#177)///
[178](https://docs.rs#178)/// [module documentation]: self
[179](https://docs.rs#179)///
[180](https://docs.rs#180)/// Some constructors accept an optional `payer`, the account responsible for
[181](https://docs.rs#181)/// paying the cost of executing a transaction. In most cases, callers should
[182](https://docs.rs#182)/// specify the payer explicitly in these constructors. In some cases though,
[183](https://docs.rs#183)/// the caller is not _required_ to specify the payer, but is still allowed to:
[184](https://docs.rs#184)/// in the [`Message`] structure, the first account is always the fee-payer, so
[185](https://docs.rs#185)/// if the caller has knowledge that the first account of the constructed
[186](https://docs.rs#186)/// transaction's `Message` is both a signer and the expected fee-payer, then
[187](https://docs.rs#187)/// redundantly specifying the fee-payer is not strictly required.
[188](https://docs.rs#188)#[cfg_attr(
[189](https://docs.rs#189)    feature = "frozen-abi",
[190](https://docs.rs#190)    derive(AbiExample, StableAbi),
[191](https://docs.rs#191)    frozen_abi(
[192](https://docs.rs#192)        api_digest = "ADDDuk3dAZJ5hDxue8v4btH7nhEyngxUpXaC7A4k8gyQ",
[193](https://docs.rs#193)        abi_digest = "nqwtny8tEU2TSSJb5Jf46fJjudMN1iWG3GnMLVLjW7X",
[194](https://docs.rs#194)        abi_serializer = "wincode"
[195](https://docs.rs#195)    )
[196](https://docs.rs#196))]
[197](https://docs.rs#197)#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(Deserialize, Serialize))]
[198](https://docs.rs#198)#[cfg_attr(feature = "wincode", derive(SchemaWrite, SchemaRead))]

[200](https://docs.rs#200)pub struct Transaction {
[201](https://docs.rs#201)    /// A set of signatures of a serialized [`Message`], signed by the first
[202](https://docs.rs#202)    /// keys of the `Message`'s [`account_keys`], where the number of signatures
[203](https://docs.rs#203)    /// is equal to [`num_required_signatures`] of the `Message`'s
[204](https://docs.rs#204)    /// [`MessageHeader`].
[205](https://docs.rs#205)    ///
[206](https://docs.rs#206)    /// [`account_keys`]: https://docs.rs/solana-message/latest/solana_message/legacy/struct.Message.html#structfield.account_keys
[207](https://docs.rs#207)    /// [`MessageHeader`]: https://docs.rs/solana-message/latest/solana_message/struct.MessageHeader.html
[208](https://docs.rs#208)    /// [`num_required_signatures`]: https://docs.rs/solana-message/latest/solana_message/struct.MessageHeader.html#structfield.num_required_signatures
[209](https://docs.rs#209)    // NOTE: Serialization-related changes must be paired with the direct read at sigverify.
[210](https://docs.rs#210)    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(with = "short_vec"))]
[211](https://docs.rs#211)    #[cfg_attr(feature = "wincode", wincode(with = "containers::Vec<_, ShortU16>"))]
[212](https://docs.rs#212)    pub signatures: Vec<Signature>,
[213](https://docs.rs#213)
[214](https://docs.rs#214)    /// The message to sign.
[215](https://docs.rs#215)    pub message: Message,
[216](https://docs.rs#216)}
[217](https://docs.rs#217)
[218](https://docs.rs#218)#[cfg(feature = "frozen-abi")]
[219](https://docs.rs#219)impl solana_frozen_abi::rand::prelude::Distribution<Transaction>
[220](https://docs.rs#220)    for solana_frozen_abi::rand::distr::StandardUniform
[221](https://docs.rs#221){
[222](https://docs.rs#222)    fn sample<R: solana_frozen_abi::rand::Rng + ?Sized>(&self, rng: &mut R) -> Transaction {
[223](https://docs.rs#223)        let signatures: Vec<Signature> = (0..rng.random_range(1..4))
[224](https://docs.rs#224)            .map(|_| Signature::from(core::array::from_fn(|_| rng.random::<u8>())))
[225](https://docs.rs#225)            .collect();
[226](https://docs.rs#226)        let accounts: Vec<AccountMeta> = (0..rng.random_range(1..6))
[227](https://docs.rs#227)            .map(|_| AccountMeta {
[228](https://docs.rs#228)                pubkey: Address::new_from_array(rng.random()),
[229](https://docs.rs#229)                is_signer: rng.random(),
[230](https://docs.rs#230)                is_writable: rng.random(),
[231](https://docs.rs#231)            })
[232](https://docs.rs#232)            .collect();
[233](https://docs.rs#233)        let data: Vec<u8> = (0..rng.random_range(1..100))
[234](https://docs.rs#234)            .map(|_| rng.random())
[235](https://docs.rs#235)            .collect();
[236](https://docs.rs#236)        let instructions: Vec<Instruction> = (0..rng.random_range(1..6))
[237](https://docs.rs#237)            .map(|_| Instruction {
[238](https://docs.rs#238)                program_id: Address::new_from_array(rng.random()),
[239](https://docs.rs#239)                accounts: accounts.clone(),
[240](https://docs.rs#240)                data: data.clone(),
[241](https://docs.rs#241)            })
[242](https://docs.rs#242)            .collect();
[243](https://docs.rs#243)
[244](https://docs.rs#244)        Transaction {
[245](https://docs.rs#245)            signatures,
[246](https://docs.rs#246)            message: Message::new(&instructions, Some(&Address::new_from_array(rng.random()))),
[247](https://docs.rs#247)        }
[248](https://docs.rs#248)    }
[249](https://docs.rs#249)}

[251](https://docs.rs#251)impl Sanitize for Transaction {
[252](https://docs.rs#252)    fn sanitize(&self) -> Result<(), SanitizeError> {
[253](https://docs.rs#253)        if self.message.header.num_required_signatures as usize > self.signatures.len() {
[254](https://docs.rs#254)            return Err(SanitizeError::IndexOutOfBounds);
[255](https://docs.rs#255)        }
[256](https://docs.rs#256)        if self.signatures.len() > self.message.account_keys.len() {
[257](https://docs.rs#257)            return Err(SanitizeError::IndexOutOfBounds);
[258](https://docs.rs#258)        }
[259](https://docs.rs#259)        self.message.sanitize()
[260](https://docs.rs#260)    }

[316](https://docs.rs#316)    ///     tx.sign(&[payer], blockhash);

[318](https://docs.rs#318)    ///

[323](https://docs.rs#323)    /// # let program_id = Pubkey::new_unique();
[324](https://docs.rs#324)    /// # let payer = Keypair::new();
[325](https://docs.rs#325)    /// # send_initialize_tx(&client, program_id, &payer)?;
[326](https://docs.rs#326)    /// #
[327](https://docs.rs#327)    /// # Ok::<(), anyhow::Error>(())
[328](https://docs.rs#328)    /// ```
[329](https://docs.rs#329)    pub fn new_unsigned(message: Message) -> Self {
[330](https://docs.rs#330)        Self {
[331](https://docs.rs#331)            signatures: vec![Signature::default(); message.header.num_required_signatures as usize],
[332](https://docs.rs#332)            message,
[333](https://docs.rs#333)        }
[334](https://docs.rs#334)    }

[407](https://docs.rs#407)    pub fn new<T: Signers + ?Sized>(

[571](https://docs.rs#571)    /// Create a fully-signed transaction from pre-compiled instructions.
[572](https://docs.rs#572)    ///
[573](https://docs.rs#573)    /// # Arguments
[574](https://docs.rs#574)    ///
[575](https://docs.rs#575)    /// * `from_keypairs` - The keys used to sign the transaction.
[576](https://docs.rs#576)    /// * `keys` - The keys for the transaction.  These are the program state
[577](https://docs.rs#577)    ///   instances or lamport recipient keys.
[578](https://docs.rs#578)    /// * `recent_blockhash` - The PoH hash.
[579](https://docs.rs#579)    /// * `program_ids` - The keys that identify programs used in the `instruction` vector.
[580](https://docs.rs#580)    /// * `instructions` - Instructions that will be executed atomically.
[581](https://docs.rs#581)    ///
[582](https://docs.rs#582)    /// # Panics
[583](https://docs.rs#583)    ///
[584](https://docs.rs#584)    /// Panics when signing fails. See [`Transaction::try_sign`] and for a full
[585](https://docs.rs#585)    /// description of failure conditions.
[586](https://docs.rs#586)    #[cfg(feature = "wincode")]
[587](https://docs.rs#587)    pub fn new_with_compiled_instructions<T: Signers + ?Sized>(
[588](https://docs.rs#588)        from_keypairs: &T,
[589](https://docs.rs#589)        keys: &[Address],
[590](https://docs.rs#590)        recent_blockhash: Hash,
[591](https://docs.rs#591)        program_ids: Vec<Address>,
[592](https://docs.rs#592)        instructions: Vec<CompiledInstruction>,
[593](https://docs.rs#593)    ) -> Self {
[594](https://docs.rs#594)        let mut account_keys = from_keypairs.pubkeys();
[595](https://docs.rs#595)        let from_keypairs_len = account_keys.len();
[596](https://docs.rs#596)        account_keys.extend_from_slice(keys);
[597](https://docs.rs#597)        account_keys.extend(&program_ids);
[598](https://docs.rs#598)        let message = Message::new_with_compiled_instructions(
[599](https://docs.rs#599)            from_keypairs_len as u8,
[600](https://docs.rs#600)            0,
[601](https://docs.rs#601)            program_ids.len() as u8,
[602](https://docs.rs#602)            account_keys,
[603](https://docs.rs#603)            Hash::default(),
[604](https://docs.rs#604)            instructions,
[605](https://docs.rs#605)        );
[606](https://docs.rs#606)        Transaction::new(from_keypairs, message, recent_blockhash)
[607](https://docs.rs#607)    }
[608](https://docs.rs#608)
[609](https://docs.rs#609)    /// Get the data for an instruction at the given index.
[610](https://docs.rs#610)    ///
[611](https://docs.rs#611)    /// The `instruction_index` corresponds to the [`instructions`] vector of
[612](https://docs.rs#612)    /// the `Transaction`'s [`Message`] value.
[613](https://docs.rs#613)    ///
[614](https://docs.rs#614)    /// [`instructions`]: Message::instructions
[615](https://docs.rs#615)    ///
[616](https://docs.rs#616)    /// # Panics
[617](https://docs.rs#617)    ///
[618](https://docs.rs#618)    /// Panics if `instruction_index` is greater than or equal to the number of
[619](https://docs.rs#619)    /// instructions in the transaction.
[620](https://docs.rs#620)    pub fn data(&self, instruction_index: usize) -> &[u8] {
[621](https://docs.rs#621)        &self.message.instructions[instruction_index].data
[622](https://docs.rs#622)    }
[623](https://docs.rs#623)
[624](https://docs.rs#624)    fn key_index(&self, instruction_index: usize, accounts_index: usize) -> Option<usize> {
[625](https://docs.rs#625)        self.message
[626](https://docs.rs#626)            .instructions
[627](https://docs.rs#627)            .get(instruction_index)
[628](https://docs.rs#628)            .and_then(|instruction| instruction.accounts.get(accounts_index))
[629](https://docs.rs#629)            .map(|&account_keys_index| account_keys_index as usize)
[630](https://docs.rs#630)    }
[631](https://docs.rs#631)
[632](https://docs.rs#632)    /// Get the `Pubkey` of an account required by one of the instructions in
[633](https://docs.rs#633)    /// the transaction.
[634](https://docs.rs#634)    ///
[635](https://docs.rs#635)    /// The `instruction_index` corresponds to the [`instructions`] vector of
[636](https://docs.rs#636)    /// the `Transaction`'s [`Message`] value; and the `account_index` to the
[637](https://docs.rs#637)    /// [`accounts`] vector of the message's [`CompiledInstruction`]s.
[638](https://docs.rs#638)    ///
[639](https://docs.rs#639)    /// [`instructions`]: Message::instructions
[640](https://docs.rs#640)    /// [`accounts`]: CompiledInstruction::accounts
[641](https://docs.rs#641)    /// [`CompiledInstruction`]: CompiledInstruction
[642](https://docs.rs#642)    ///
[643](https://docs.rs#643)    /// Returns `None` if `instruction_index` is greater than or equal to the
[644](https://docs.rs#644)    /// number of instructions in the transaction; or if `accounts_index` is
[645](https://docs.rs#645)    /// greater than or equal to the number of accounts in the instruction.
[646](https://docs.rs#646)    pub fn key(&self, instruction_index: usize, accounts_index: usize) -> Option<&Address> {
[647](https://docs.rs#647)        self.key_index(instruction_index, accounts_index)
[648](https://docs.rs#648)            .and_then(|account_keys_index| self.message.account_keys.get(account_keys_index))
[649](https://docs.rs#649)    }
[650](https://docs.rs#650)
[651](https://docs.rs#651)    /// Get the `Pubkey` of a signing account required by one of the
[652](https://docs.rs#652)    /// instructions in the transaction.
[653](https://docs.rs#653)    ///
[654](https://docs.rs#654)    /// The transaction does not need to be signed for this function to return a
[655](https://docs.rs#655)    /// signing account's pubkey.
[656](https://docs.rs#656)    ///
[657](https://docs.rs#657)    /// Returns `None` if the indexed account is not required to sign the
[658](https://docs.rs#658)    /// transaction. Returns `None` if the [`signatures`] field does not contain
[659](https://docs.rs#659)    /// enough elements to hold a signature for the indexed account (this should
[660](https://docs.rs#660)    /// only be possible if `Transaction` has been manually constructed).
[661](https://docs.rs#661)    ///
[662](https://docs.rs#662)    /// [`signatures`]: Transaction::signatures
[663](https://docs.rs#663)    ///
[664](https://docs.rs#664)    /// Returns `None` if `instruction_index` is greater than or equal to the
[665](https://docs.rs#665)    /// number of instructions in the transaction; or if `accounts_index` is
[666](https://docs.rs#666)    /// greater than or equal to the number of accounts in the instruction.
[667](https://docs.rs#667)    pub fn signer_key(&self, instruction_index: usize, accounts_index: usize) -> Option<&Address> {
[668](https://docs.rs#668)        match self.key_index(instruction_index, accounts_index) {
[669](https://docs.rs#669)            None => None,
[670](https://docs.rs#670)            Some(signature_index) => {
[671](https://docs.rs#671)                if signature_index >= self.signatures.len() {
[672](https://docs.rs#672)                    return None;
[673](https://docs.rs#673)                }
[674](https://docs.rs#674)                self.message.account_keys.get(signature_index)
[675](https://docs.rs#675)            }
[676](https://docs.rs#676)        }
[677](https://docs.rs#677)    }
[678](https://docs.rs#678)
[679](https://docs.rs#679)    /// Return the message containing all data that should be signed.
[680](https://docs.rs#680)    pub fn message(&self) -> &Message {
[681](https://docs.rs#681)        &self.message

[690](https://docs.rs#690)    /// Sign the transaction.

[692](https://docs.rs#692)    /// This method fully signs a transaction with all required signers, which
[693](https://docs.rs#693)    /// must be present in the `keypairs` slice. To sign with only some of the
[694](https://docs.rs#694)    /// required signers, use [`Transaction::partial_sign`].

[825](https://docs.rs#825)    /// Sign the transaction, returning any errors.
[826](https://docs.rs#826)    ///
[827](https://docs.rs#827)    /// This method fully signs a transaction with all required signers, which
[828](https://docs.rs#828)    /// must be present in the `keypairs` slice. To sign with only some of the
[829](https://docs.rs#829)    /// required signers, use [`Transaction::try_partial_sign`].
[830](https://docs.rs#830)    ///
[831](https://docs.rs#831)    /// If `recent_blockhash` is different than recorded in the transaction message's
[832](https://docs.rs#832)    /// [`recent_blockhash`] field, then the message's `recent_blockhash` will be updated
[833](https://docs.rs#833)    /// to the provided `recent_blockhash`, and any prior signatures will be cleared.

[836](https://docs.rs#836)    ///
[837](https://docs.rs#837)    /// # Errors
[838](https://docs.rs#838)    ///
[839](https://docs.rs#839)    /// Signing will fail if some required signers are not provided in
[840](https://docs.rs#840)    /// `keypairs`; or, if the transaction has previously been partially signed,
[841](https://docs.rs#841)    /// some of the remaining required signers are not provided in `keypairs`.
[842](https://docs.rs#842)    /// In other words, the transaction must be fully signed as a result of
[843](https://docs.rs#843)    /// calling this function. The error is [`SignerError::NotEnoughSigners`].
[844](https://docs.rs#844)    ///
[845](https://docs.rs#845)    /// Signing will fail for any of the reasons described in the documentation
[846](https://docs.rs#846)    /// for [`Transaction::try_partial_sign`].
[847](https://docs.rs#847)    ///

[899](https://docs.rs#899)    /// # let client = RpcClient::new(String::new());
[900](https://docs.rs#900)    /// # let program_id = Pubkey::new_unique();
[901](https://docs.rs#901)    /// # let payer = Keypair::new();
[902](https://docs.rs#902)    /// # send_initialize_tx(&client, program_id, &payer)?;
[903](https://docs.rs#903)    /// #
[904](https://docs.rs#904)    /// # Ok::<(), anyhow::Error>(())
[905](https://docs.rs#905)    /// ```
[906](https://docs.rs#906)    #[cfg(feature = "wincode")]
[907](https://docs.rs#907)    pub fn try_sign<T: Signers + ?Sized>(
[908](https://docs.rs#908)        &mut self,
[909](https://docs.rs#909)        keypairs: &T,
[910](https://docs.rs#910)        recent_blockhash: Hash,
[911](https://docs.rs#911)    ) -> Result<(), SignerError> {
[912](https://docs.rs#912)        self.try_partial_sign(keypairs, recent_blockhash)?;
[913](https://docs.rs#913)
[914](https://docs.rs#914)        if !self.is_signed() {
[915](https://docs.rs#915)            Err(SignerError::NotEnoughSigners)
[916](https://docs.rs#916)        } else {
[917](https://docs.rs#917)            Ok(())
[918](https://docs.rs#918)        }
[919](https://docs.rs#919)    }

[921](https://docs.rs#921)    /// Sign the transaction with a subset of required keys, returning any errors.
[922](https://docs.rs#922)    ///
[923](https://docs.rs#923)    /// Unlike [`Transaction::try_sign`], this method does not require all
[924](https://docs.rs#924)    /// keypairs to be provided, allowing a transaction to be signed in multiple
[925](https://docs.rs#925)    /// steps.
[926](https://docs.rs#926)    ///
[927](https://docs.rs#927)    /// It is permitted to sign a transaction with the same keypair multiple
[928](https://docs.rs#928)    /// times.
[929](https://docs.rs#929)    ///
[930](https://docs.rs#930)    /// If `recent_blockhash` is different than recorded in the transaction message's
[931](https://docs.rs#931)    /// [`recent_blockhash`] field, then the message's `recent_blockhash` will be updated
[932](https://docs.rs#932)    /// to the provided `recent_blockhash`, and any prior signatures will be cleared.
[933](https://docs.rs#933)    ///
[934](https://docs.rs#934)    /// [`recent_blockhash`]: Message::recent_blockhash
[935](https://docs.rs#935)    ///
[936](https://docs.rs#936)    /// # Errors
[937](https://docs.rs#937)    ///
[938](https://docs.rs#938)    /// Signing will fail if
[939](https://docs.rs#939)    ///
[940](https://docs.rs#940)    /// - The transaction's [`Message`] is malformed such that the number of
[941](https://docs.rs#941)    ///   required signatures recorded in its header
[942](https://docs.rs#942)    ///   ([`num_required_signatures`]) is greater than the length of its
[943](https://docs.rs#943)    ///   account keys ([`account_keys`]). The error is
[944](https://docs.rs#944)    ///   [`SignerError::TransactionError`] where the interior
[945](https://docs.rs#945)    ///   [`TransactionError`] is [`TransactionError::InvalidAccountIndex`].
[946](https://docs.rs#946)    /// - Any of the provided signers in `keypairs` is not a required signer of
[947](https://docs.rs#947)    ///   the message. The error is [`SignerError::KeypairPubkeyMismatch`].
[948](https://docs.rs#948)    /// - Any of the signers is a [`Presigner`], and its provided signature is
[949](https://docs.rs#949)    ///   incorrect. The error is [`SignerError::PresignerError`] where the
[950](https://docs.rs#950)    ///   interior [`PresignerError`] is
[951](https://docs.rs#951)    ///   [`PresignerError::VerificationFailure`].
[952](https://docs.rs#952)    /// - The signer is a [`RemoteKeypair`] and
[953](https://docs.rs#953)    ///   - It does not understand the input provided ([`SignerError::InvalidInput`]).
[954](https://docs.rs#954)    ///   - The device cannot be found ([`SignerError::NoDeviceFound`]).
[955](https://docs.rs#955)    ///   - The user cancels the signing ([`SignerError::UserCancel`]).
[956](https://docs.rs#956)    ///   - An error was encountered connecting ([`SignerError::Connection`]).
[957](https://docs.rs#957)    ///   - Some device-specific protocol error occurs ([`SignerError::Protocol`]).
[958](https://docs.rs#958)    ///   - Some other error occurs ([`SignerError::Custom`]).
[959](https://docs.rs#959)    ///
[960](https://docs.rs#960)    /// See the documentation for the [`solana-remote-wallet`] crate for details
[961](https://docs.rs#961)    /// on the operation of [`RemoteKeypair`] signers.
[962](https://docs.rs#962)    ///
[963](https://docs.rs#963)    /// [`num_required_signatures`]: https://docs.rs/solana-message/latest/solana_message/struct.MessageHeader.html#structfield.num_required_signatures
[964](https://docs.rs#964)    /// [`account_keys`]: https://docs.rs/solana-message/latest/solana_message/legacy/struct.Message.html#structfield.account_keys
[965](https://docs.rs#965)    /// [`Presigner`]: https://docs.rs/solana-presigner/latest/solana_presigner/struct.Presigner.html
[966](https://docs.rs#966)    /// [`PresignerError`]: https://docs.rs/solana-signer/latest/solana_signer/enum.PresignerError.html
[967](https://docs.rs#967)    /// [`PresignerError::VerificationFailure`]: https://docs.rs/solana-signer/latest/solana_signer/enum.PresignerError.html#variant.WrongSize
[968](https://docs.rs#968)    /// [`solana-remote-wallet`]: https://docs.rs/solana-remote-wallet/latest/
[969](https://docs.rs#969)    /// [`RemoteKeypair`]: https://docs.rs/solana-remote-wallet/latest/solana_remote_wallet/remote_keypair/struct.RemoteKeypair.html
[970](https://docs.rs#970)    #[cfg(feature = "wincode")]
[971](https://docs.rs#971)    pub fn try_partial_sign<T: Signers + ?Sized>(
[972](https://docs.rs#972)        &mut self,
[973](https://docs.rs#973)        keypairs: &T,
[974](https://docs.rs#974)        recent_blockhash: Hash,
[975](https://docs.rs#975)    ) -> Result<(), SignerError> {
[976](https://docs.rs#976)        let positions: Vec<usize> = self
[977](https://docs.rs#977)            .get_signing_keypair_positions(&keypairs.pubkeys())?
[978](https://docs.rs#978)            .into_iter()
[979](https://docs.rs#979)            .collect::<Option<_>>()
[980](https://docs.rs#980)            .ok_or(SignerError::KeypairPubkeyMismatch)?;
[981](https://docs.rs#981)        self.try_partial_sign_unchecked(keypairs, positions, recent_blockhash)
[982](https://docs.rs#982)    }
[983](https://docs.rs#983)
[984](https://docs.rs#984)    /// Sign the transaction with a subset of required keys, returning any
[985](https://docs.rs#985)    /// errors.
[986](https://docs.rs#986)    ///
[987](https://docs.rs#987)    /// This places each of the signatures created from `keypairs` in the
[988](https://docs.rs#988)    /// corresponding position, as specified in the `positions` vector, in the
[989](https://docs.rs#989)    /// transactions [`signatures`] field. It does not verify that the signature
[990](https://docs.rs#990)    /// positions are correct.
[991](https://docs.rs#991)    ///
[992](https://docs.rs#992)    /// [`signatures`]: Transaction::signatures
[993](https://docs.rs#993)    ///
[994](https://docs.rs#994)    /// # Errors
[995](https://docs.rs#995)    ///
[996](https://docs.rs#996)    /// Returns an error if signing fails.
[997](https://docs.rs#997)    #[cfg(feature = "wincode")]
[998](https://docs.rs#998)    pub fn try_partial_sign_unchecked<T: Signers + ?Sized>(
[999](https://docs.rs#999)        &mut self,
[1000](https://docs.rs#1000)        keypairs: &T,
[1001](https://docs.rs#1001)        positions: Vec<usize>,
[1002](https://docs.rs#1002)        recent_blockhash: Hash,
[1003](https://docs.rs#1003)    ) -> Result<(), SignerError> {
[1004](https://docs.rs#1004)        // if you change the blockhash, you're re-signing...
[1005](https://docs.rs#1005)        if recent_blockhash != self.message.recent_blockhash {
[1006](https://docs.rs#1006)            self.message.recent_blockhash = recent_blockhash;

[1072](https://docs.rs#1072)    pub(crate) fn _verify_with_results(&self, message_bytes: &[u8]) -> Vec<bool> {
[1073](https://docs.rs#1073)        self.signatures

[1075](https://docs.rs#1075)            .zip(&self.message.account_keys)

[1083](https://docs.rs#1083)    pub fn get_signing_keypair_positions(

[1100](https://docs.rs#1100)    /// Replace all the signatures and pubkeys.
[1101](https://docs.rs#1101)    pub fn replace_signatures(
[1102](https://docs.rs#1102)        &mut self,
[1103](https://docs.rs#1103)        signers: &[(Address, Signature)],
[1104](https://docs.rs#1104)    ) -> TransactionResult<()> {
[1105](https://docs.rs#1105)        let num_required_signatures = self.message.header.num_required_signatures as usize;
[1106](https://docs.rs#1106)        if signers.len() != num_required_signatures
[1107](https://docs.rs#1107)            || self.signatures.len() != num_required_signatures
[1108](https://docs.rs#1108)            || self.message.account_keys.len() < num_required_signatures
[1109](https://docs.rs#1109)        {
[1110](https://docs.rs#1110)            return Err(TransactionError::InvalidAccountIndex);
[1111](https://docs.rs#1111)        }
[1112](https://docs.rs#1112)
[1113](https://docs.rs#1113)        for (index, account_key) in self
[1114](https://docs.rs#1114)            .message
[1115](https://docs.rs#1115)            .account_keys
[1116](https://docs.rs#1116)            .iter()
[1117](https://docs.rs#1117)            .enumerate()
[1118](https://docs.rs#1118)            .take(num_required_signatures)
[1119](https://docs.rs#1119)        {
[1120](https://docs.rs#1120)            if let Some((_pubkey, signature)) =
[1121](https://docs.rs#1121)                signers.iter().find(|(key, _signature)| account_key == key)
[1122](https://docs.rs#1122)            {
[1123](https://docs.rs#1123)                self.signatures[index] = *signature
[1124](https://docs.rs#1124)            } else {
[1125](https://docs.rs#1125)                return Err(TransactionError::InvalidAccountIndex);
[1126](https://docs.rs#1126)            }
[1127](https://docs.rs#1127)        }
[1128](https://docs.rs#1128)
[1129](https://docs.rs#1129)        self.verify()
[1130](https://docs.rs#1130)    }

[1348](https://docs.rs#1348)    /// Detect changes to the serialized size of payment transactions, which affects TPS.
[1349](https://docs.rs#1349)    #[test]
[1350](https://docs.rs#1350)    fn test_transaction_minimum_serialized_size() {
[1351](https://docs.rs#1351)        let alice_keypair = Keypair::new();
[1352](https://docs.rs#1352)        let alice_pubkey = alice_keypair.pubkey();
[1353](https://docs.rs#1353)        let bob_pubkey = solana_pubkey::new_rand();
[1354](https://docs.rs#1354)        let ix = system_instruction::transfer(&alice_pubkey, &bob_pubkey, 42);
[1355](https://docs.rs#1355)
[1356](https://docs.rs#1356)        let expected_data_size = size_of::<u32>() + size_of::<u64>();
[1357](https://docs.rs#1357)        assert_eq!(expected_data_size, 12);
[1358](https://docs.rs#1358)        assert_eq!(
[1359](https://docs.rs#1359)            ix.data.len(),
[1360](https://docs.rs#1360)            expected_data_size,
[1361](https://docs.rs#1361)            "unexpected system instruction size"
[1362](https://docs.rs#1362)        );
[1363](https://docs.rs#1363)
[1364](https://docs.rs#1364)        let expected_instruction_size = 1 + 1 + ix.accounts.len() + 1 + expected_data_size;
[1365](https://docs.rs#1365)        assert_eq!(expected_instruction_size, 17);
[1366](https://docs.rs#1366)
[1367](https://docs.rs#1367)        let message = Message::new(&[ix], Some(&alice_pubkey));
[1368](https://docs.rs#1368)        assert_eq!(
[1369](https://docs.rs#1369)            serialized_size(&message.instructions[0]).unwrap() as usize,
[1370](https://docs.rs#1370)            expected_instruction_size,
[1371](https://docs.rs#1371)            "unexpected Instruction::serialized_size"
[1372](https://docs.rs#1372)        );
[1373](https://docs.rs#1373)
[1374](https://docs.rs#1374)        let tx = Transaction::new(&[&alice_keypair], message, Hash::default());
[1375](https://docs.rs#1375)
[1376](https://docs.rs#1376)        let len_size = 1;
[1377](https://docs.rs#1377)        let num_required_sigs_size = 1;
[1378](https://docs.rs#1378)        let num_readonly_accounts_size = 2;
[1379](https://docs.rs#1379)        let blockhash_size = size_of::<Hash>();
[1380](https://docs.rs#1380)        let expected_transaction_size = len_size
[1381](https://docs.rs#1381)            + (tx.signatures.len() * size_of::<Signature>())
[1382](https://docs.rs#1382)            + num_required_sigs_size
[1383](https://docs.rs#1383)            + num_readonly_accounts_size
[1384](https://docs.rs#1384)            + len_size
[1385](https://docs.rs#1385)            + (tx.message.account_keys.len() * size_of::<Address>())
[1386](https://docs.rs#1386)            + blockhash_size
[1387](https://docs.rs#1387)            + len_size
[1388](https://docs.rs#1388)            + expected_instruction_size;
[1389](https://docs.rs#1389)        assert_eq!(expected_transaction_size, 215);
[1390](https://docs.rs#1390)
[1391](https://docs.rs#1391)        assert_eq!(
[1392](https://docs.rs#1392)            serialized_size(&tx).unwrap() as usize,
[1393](https://docs.rs#1393)            expected_transaction_size,
[1394](https://docs.rs#1394)            "unexpected serialized transaction size"
[1395](https://docs.rs#1395)        );
[1396](https://docs.rs#1396)    }

[1536](https://docs.rs#1536)    fn test_try_sign_dyn_keypairs() {
[1537](https://docs.rs#1537)        let program_id = Address::default();
[1538](https://docs.rs#1538)        let keypair = Keypair::new();
[1539](https://docs.rs#1539)        let pubkey = keypair.pubkey();
[1540](https://docs.rs#1540)        let presigner_keypair = Keypair::new();
[1541](https://docs.rs#1541)        let presigner_pubkey = presigner_keypair.pubkey();
[1542](https://docs.rs#1542)
[1543](https://docs.rs#1543)        let ix = Instruction::new_with_bincode(
[1544](https://docs.rs#1544)            program_id,
[1545](https://docs.rs#1545)            &0,
[1546](https://docs.rs#1546)            vec![
[1547](https://docs.rs#1547)                AccountMeta::new(pubkey, true),
[1548](https://docs.rs#1548)                AccountMeta::new(presigner_pubkey, true),
[1549](https://docs.rs#1549)            ],
[1550](https://docs.rs#1550)        );
[1551](https://docs.rs#1551)        let message = Message::new(&[ix], Some(&pubkey));
[1552](https://docs.rs#1552)        let mut tx = Transaction::new_unsigned(message);
[1553](https://docs.rs#1553)

[1556](https://docs.rs#1556)

[1558](https://docs.rs#1558)

[1560](https://docs.rs#1560)        assert_eq!(res, Ok(()));
[1561](https://docs.rs#1561)        assert_eq!(tx.signatures[0], keypair.sign_message(&tx.message_data()));
[1562](https://docs.rs#1562)        assert_eq!(tx.signatures[1], presigner_sig);
[1563](https://docs.rs#1563)
[1564](https://docs.rs#1564)        // Wrong key should error, not panic
[1565](https://docs.rs#1565)        let another_pubkey = solana_pubkey::new_rand();
[1566](https://docs.rs#1566)        let ix = Instruction::new_with_bincode(
[1567](https://docs.rs#1567)            program_id,
[1568](https://docs.rs#1568)            &0,

[1572](https://docs.rs#1572)            ],
[1573](https://docs.rs#1573)        );
[1574](https://docs.rs#1574)        let message = Message::new(&[ix], Some(&another_pubkey));

[1579](https://docs.rs#1579)        assert_eq!(

# Instruction in solana_transaction - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/solana-transaction/4.1.5/solana_transaction/struct.Instruction.html

```
pub struct Instruction {
    pub program_id:
```
[Address](https://docs.rs/struct.Address.html),
    pub accounts: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[AccountMeta](https://docs.rs/struct.AccountMeta.html)>,
    pub data: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)>,
}## Expand description

A directive for a single invocation of a Solana program.

An instruction specifies which program it is calling, which accounts it may
read or modify, and additional data that serves as input to the program. One
or more instructions are included in transactions submitted by Solana
clients. Instructions are also used to describe [cross-program
invocations](https://solana.com/docs/core/cpi).

During execution, a program will receive a list of account data as one of
its arguments, in the same order as specified during `Instruction`
construction.

While Solana is agnostic to the format of the instruction data, it has
built-in support for serialization via [ borsh](https://docs.rs/borsh/latest/borsh/) and

[.](https://docs.rs/bincode/latest/bincode/)

`bincode`[§](https://docs.rs#specifying-account-metadata)Specifying account metadata

When constructing an [ Instruction](https://docs.rs/struct.Instruction.html), a list of all accounts that may be
read or written during the execution of that instruction must be supplied as

[values.](https://docs.rs/struct.AccountMeta.html)

`AccountMeta`Any account whose data may be mutated by the program during execution must be specified as writable. During execution, writing to an account that was not specified as writable will cause the transaction to fail. Writing to an account that is not owned by the program will cause the transaction to fail.

Any account whose lamport balance may be mutated by the program during
execution must be specified as writable. During execution, mutating the
lamports of an account that was not specified as writable will cause the
transaction to fail. While *subtracting* lamports from an account not owned
by the program will cause the transaction to fail, *adding* lamports to any
account is allowed, as long is it is mutable.

Accounts that are not read or written by the program may still be specified
in an `Instruction`’s account list. These will affect scheduling of program
execution by the runtime, but will otherwise be ignored.

When building a transaction, the Solana runtime coalesces all accounts used
by all instructions in that transaction, along with accounts and permissions
required by the runtime, into a single account list. Some accounts and
account permissions required by the runtime to process a transaction are
*not* required to be included in an `Instruction`s account list. These
include:

- The program ID — it is a separate field of `Instruction`
- The transaction’s fee-paying account — it is added during `Message`

Programs may require signatures from some accounts, in which case they
should be specified as signers during `Instruction` construction. The
program must still validate during execution that the account is a signer.

    program_id: [Address](https://docs.rs/struct.Address.html),
    data: &[[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)],
    accounts: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[AccountMeta](https://docs.rs/struct.AccountMeta.html)>,
) -> [Instruction](https://docs.rs/struct.Instruction.html)

Create a new instruction from a byte slice.

`program_id` is the address of the program that will execute the instruction.
`accounts` contains a description of all accounts that may be accessed by the program.

The caller is responsible for ensuring the correct encoding of `data` as expected
by the callee program.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
#[derive(BorshSerialize, BorshDeserialize)]
pub struct MyInstruction {
    pub lamports: u64,
}
pub fn create_instruction(
    program_id: &Pubkey,
    from: &Pubkey,
    to: &Pubkey,
    lamports: u64,
) -> Result<Instruction, Error> {
    let instr = MyInstruction { lamports };
    let mut instr_in_bytes: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
    instr.serialize(&mut instr_in_bytes)?;
    Ok(Instruction::new_with_bytes(
        *program_id,
        &instr_in_bytes,
        vec![
            AccountMeta::new(*from, true),
            AccountMeta::new(*to, false),
        ],
   ))
}
```

# Transaction in solana_transaction - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/solana-transaction/4.1.5/solana_transaction/struct.Transaction.html

## Expand description

An atomically-committed sequence of instructions.

While [ Instruction](https://docs.rs/struct.Instruction.html)s are the basic unit of computation in Solana,
they are submitted by clients in

[s containing one or more instructions, and signed by one or more](https://docs.rs/struct.Transaction.html)

`Transaction`[s.](https://docs.rs/solana-signer/latest/solana_signer/trait.Signer.html)

`Signer`See the [module documentation](https://docs.rs/index.html) for more details about transactions.

Some constructors accept an optional `payer`, the account responsible for
paying the cost of executing a transaction. In most cases, callers should
specify the payer explicitly in these constructors. In some cases though,
the caller is not *required* to specify the payer, but is still allowed to:
in the [ Message](https://docs.rs/struct.Message.html) structure, the first account is always the fee-payer, so
if the caller has knowledge that the first account of the constructed
transaction’s

`Message` is both a signer and the expected fee-payer, then
redundantly specifying the fee-payer is not strictly required.## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

keys of the

`Message`’s [, where the number of signatures is equal to](https://docs.rs/solana-message/latest/solana_message/legacy/struct.Message.html#structfield.account_keys)

#### pub fn [new_unsigned](https://docs.rs#method.new_unsigned)(message: [Message](https://docs.rs/struct.Message.html)) -> Self

Create an unsigned transaction from a [ Message](https://docs.rs/struct.Message.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

This example uses the [ solana_rpc_client](https://docs.rs/solana-rpc-client) and

[crates.](https://docs.rs/anyhow)

`anyhow````
use anyhow::Result;
use borsh::{BorshSerialize, BorshDeserialize};
use solana_instruction::Instruction;
use solana_keypair::Keypair;
use solana_message::Message;
use solana_pubkey::Pubkey;
use solana_rpc_client::rpc_client::RpcClient;
use solana_signer::Signer;
use solana_transaction::Transaction;
// A custom program instruction. This would typically be defined in
// another crate so it can be shared between the on-chain program and
// the client.
#[derive(BorshSerialize, BorshDeserialize)]
enum BankInstruction {
    Initialize,
    Deposit { lamports: u64 },
    Withdraw { lamports: u64 },
}
fn send_initialize_tx(
    client: &RpcClient,
    program_id: Pubkey,
    payer: &Keypair
) -> Result<()> {
    let bank_instruction = BankInstruction::Initialize;
    let instruction = Instruction::new_with_borsh(
        program_id,
        &bank_instruction,
        vec![],
    );
    let message = Message::new(
        &[instruction],
        Some(&payer.pubkey()),
    );
    let mut tx = Transaction::new_unsigned(message);
    let blockhash = client.get_latest_blockhash()?;
    tx.sign(&[payer], blockhash);
    client.send_and_confirm_transaction(&tx)?;
    Ok(())
}

`wincode`Create a fully-signed transaction from a list of [ Instruction](https://docs.rs/struct.Instruction.html)s.

transaction. It is typically provided, but is optional in some cases.

`Transaction::try_partial_sign`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-3)Examples

This example uses the [ solana_rpc_client](https://docs.rs/solana-rpc-client) and

[crates.](https://docs.rs/anyhow)

`anyhow````
use anyhow::Result;
use borsh::{BorshSerialize, BorshDeserialize};
use solana_instruction::Instruction;
use solana_keypair::Keypair;
use solana_message::Message;
use solana_pubkey::Pubkey;
use solana_rpc_client::rpc_client::RpcClient;
use solana_signer::Signer;
use solana_transaction::Transaction;
// A custom program instruction. This would typically be defined in
// another crate so it can be shared between the on-chain program and
// the client.
#[derive(BorshSerialize, BorshDeserialize)]
enum BankInstruction {
    Initialize,
    Deposit { lamports: u64 },
    Withdraw { lamports: u64 },
}
fn send_initialize_tx(
    client: &RpcClient,
    program_id: Pubkey,
    payer: &Keypair
) -> Result<()> {
    let bank_instruction = BankInstruction::Initialize;
    let instruction = Instruction::new_with_borsh(
        program_id,
        &bank_instruction,
        vec![],
    );
    let blockhash = client.get_latest_blockhash()?;
    let mut tx = Transaction::new_signed_with_payer(
        &[instruction],
        Some(&payer.pubkey()),
        &[payer],
        blockhash,
    );
    client.send_and_confirm_transaction(&tx)?;
    Ok(())
}

`wincode`Sign the transaction with a subset of required keys.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/solana_transaction/lib.rs.html#907-919)

**crate feature**only.

`wincode`Sign the transaction, returning any errors.

This method fully signs a transaction with all required signers, which
must be present in the `keypairs` slice. To sign with only some of the
required signers, use [ Transaction::try_partial_sign](https://docs.rs/struct.Transaction.html#method.try_partial_sign).

If `recent_blockhash` is different than recorded in the transaction message’s
[ recent_blockhash](https://docs.rs/struct.Message.html#structfield.recent_blockhash) field, then the message’s

`recent_blockhash` will be updated
to the provided `recent_blockhash`, and any prior signatures will be cleared.[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

Signing will fail if some required signers are not provided in
`keypairs`; or, if the transaction has previously been partially signed,
some of the remaining required signers are not provided in `keypairs`.
In other words, the transaction must be fully signed as a result of
calling this function. The error is [ SignerError::NotEnoughSigners](https://docs.rs/enum.SignerError.html#variant.NotEnoughSigners).

Signing will fail for any of the reasons described in the documentation
for [ Transaction::try_partial_sign](https://docs.rs/struct.Transaction.html#method.try_partial_sign).

    pub instructions: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[CompiledInstruction](https://docs.rs/struct.CompiledInstruction.html)>,
}## Expand description

A Solana transaction message (legacy).

See the crate documentation for further description.

Some constructors accept an optional `payer`, the account responsible for
paying the cost of executing a transaction. In most cases, callers should
specify the payer explicitly in these constructors. In some cases though,
the caller is not *required* to specify the payer, but is still allowed to:
in the `Message` structure, the first account is always the fee-payer, so if
the caller has knowledge that the first account of the constructed
transaction’s `Message` is both a signer and the expected fee-payer, then
redundantly specifying the fee-payer is not strictly required.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Create a new `Message`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

This example uses the [ solana_sdk](https://docs.rs/solana-sdk),

[and](https://docs.rs/solana-rpc-client)

`solana_rpc_client`[crates.](https://docs.rs/anyhow)

`anyhow````
use anyhow::Result;
use borsh::{BorshSerialize, BorshDeserialize};
use solana_instruction::Instruction;
use solana_keypair::Keypair;
use solana_message::Message;
use solana_address::Address;
use solana_rpc_client::rpc_client::RpcClient;
use solana_signer::Signer;
use solana_transaction::Transaction;
// A custom program instruction. This would typically be defined in
// another crate so it can be shared between the on-chain program and
// the client.
#[derive(BorshSerialize, BorshDeserialize)]
enum BankInstruction {
    Initialize,
    Deposit { lamports: u64 },
    Withdraw { lamports: u64 },
}
fn send_initialize_tx(
    client: &RpcClient,
    program_id: Address,
    payer: &Keypair
) -> Result<()> {
    let bank_instruction = BankInstruction::Initialize;
    let instruction = Instruction::new_with_borsh(
        program_id,
        &bank_instruction,
        vec![],
    );
    let message = Message::new(
        &[instruction],
        Some(&payer.pubkey()),
    );
    let blockhash = client.get_latest_blockhash()?;
    let mut tx = Transaction::new(&[payer], message, blockhash);
    client.send_and_confirm_transaction(&tx)?;
    Ok(())
}

use anyhow::Result;
use borsh::{BorshSerialize, BorshDeserialize};
use solana_instruction::Instruction;
use solana_keypair::Keypair;
use solana_message::Message;
use solana_address::Address;
use solana_rpc_client::rpc_client::RpcClient;
use solana_signer::Signer;
use solana_transaction::Transaction;
// A custom program instruction. This would typically be defined in
// another crate so it can be shared between the on-chain program and
// the client.
#[derive(BorshSerialize, BorshDeserialize)]
enum BankInstruction {
    Initialize,
    Deposit { lamports: u64 },
    Withdraw { lamports: u64 },
}
fn send_initialize_tx(
    client: &RpcClient,
    program_id: Address,
    payer: &Keypair
) -> Result<()> {
    let bank_instruction = BankInstruction::Initialize;
    let instruction = Instruction::new_with_borsh(
        program_id,
        &bank_instruction,
        vec![],
    );
    let blockhash = client.get_latest_blockhash()?;
    let message = Message::new_with_blockhash(
        &[instruction],
        Some(&payer.pubkey()),
        &blockhash,
    );
    let mut tx = Transaction::new_unsigned(message);
    tx.sign(&[payer], blockhash);
    client.send_and_confirm_transaction(&tx)?;
    Ok(())
}

#### pub fn [new_with_nonce](https://docs.rs#method.new_with_nonce)(
    instructions: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[Instruction](https://docs.rs/struct.Instruction.html)>,

Create a new message for a [nonced transaction](https://docs.solanalabs.com/implemented-proposals/durable-tx-nonces).

In this type of transaction, the blockhash is replaced with a *durable
transaction nonce*, allowing for extended time to pass between the
transaction’s signing and submission to the blockchain.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-2)Examples

This example uses the [ solana_sdk](https://docs.rs/solana-sdk),

[and](https://docs.rs/solana-client)

`solana_rpc_client`[crates.](https://docs.rs/anyhow)

`anyhow````
use anyhow::Result;
use borsh::{BorshSerialize, BorshDeserialize};
use solana_hash::Hash;
use solana_instruction::Instruction;
use solana_keypair::Keypair;
use solana_message::Message;
use solana_address::Address;
use solana_rpc_client::rpc_client::RpcClient;
use solana_signer::Signer;
use solana_transaction::Transaction;
use solana_system_interface::instruction::create_nonce_account;
// A custom program instruction. This would typically be defined in
// another crate so it can be shared between the on-chain program and
// the client.
#[derive(BorshSerialize, BorshDeserialize)]
enum BankInstruction {
    Initialize,
    Deposit { lamports: u64 },
    Withdraw { lamports: u64 },
}
// Create a nonced transaction for later signing and submission,
// returning it and the nonce account's pubkey.
fn create_offline_initialize_tx(
    client: &RpcClient,
    program_id: Address,
    payer: &Keypair
) -> Result<(Transaction, Address)> {
    let bank_instruction = BankInstruction::Initialize;
    let bank_instruction = Instruction::new_with_borsh(
        program_id,
        &bank_instruction,
        vec![],
    );
    // This will create a nonce account and assign authority to the
    // payer so they can sign to advance the nonce and withdraw its rent.
    let nonce_account = make_nonce_account(client, payer)?;
    let mut message = Message::new_with_nonce(
        vec![bank_instruction],
        Some(&payer.pubkey()),
        &nonce_account,
        &payer.pubkey()
    );
    // This transaction will need to be signed later, using the blockhash
    // stored in the nonce account.
    let tx = Transaction::new_unsigned(message);
    Ok((tx, nonce_account))
}
fn make_nonce_account(client: &RpcClient, payer: &Keypair)
    -> Result<Address>
{
    let nonce_account_address = Keypair::new();
    let nonce_account_size = solana_nonce::state::State::size();
    let nonce_rent = client.get_minimum_balance_for_rent_exemption(nonce_account_size)?;
    // Assigning the nonce authority to the payer so they can sign for the withdrawal,
    // and we can throw away the nonce address secret key.
    let create_nonce_instr = create_nonce_account(
        &payer.pubkey(),
        &nonce_account_address.pubkey(),
        &payer.pubkey(),
        nonce_rent,
    );
    let mut nonce_tx = Transaction::new_with_payer(&create_nonce_instr, Some(&payer.pubkey()));
    let blockhash = client.get_latest_blockhash()?;
    nonce_tx.sign(&[&payer, &nonce_account_address], blockhash);
    client.send_and_confirm_transaction(&nonce_tx)?;
    Ok(nonce_account_address.pubkey())
}

# solana_transaction::containers - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/solana-transaction/4.1.5/solana_transaction/containers/index.html

**crate feature**only.

`wincode`## Expand description

This module provides specialized implementations of standard library collection types that
provide control over the length encoding (see [ SeqLen](https://docs.rs/wincode/0.5.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/wincode/len/trait.SeqLen.html)), as well
as special case opt-in raw-copy overrides (see

[).](https://docs.rs/macro.pod_wrapper.html)

`pod_wrapper!`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Raw byte vec with solana short vec length encoding:

```
#[derive(Serialize, SchemaWrite)]
struct MyStruct {
    #[serde(with = "solana_short_vec")]
    #[wincode(with = "containers::Vec<_, ShortU16>")]
    vec: Vec<u8>,
}
let my_struct = MyStruct {
    vec: vec![1, 2, 3],
};
let wincode_bytes = wincode::serialize(&my_struct).unwrap();
let bincode_bytes = bincode::serialize(&my_struct).unwrap();
assert_eq!(wincode_bytes, bincode_bytes);
```
Vector with struct elements and custom length encoding:

```
#[derive(Serialize, SchemaWrite)]
struct Point {
    x: u64,
    y: u64,
}
#[derive(Serialize, SchemaWrite)]
struct MyStruct {
    #[serde(with = "solana_short_vec")]
    #[wincode(with = "containers::Vec<Point, ShortU16>")]
    vec: Vec<Point>,
}
let my_struct = MyStruct {
    vec: vec![Point { x: 1, y: 2 }, Point { x: 3, y: 4 }],
};
let wincode_bytes = wincode::serialize(&my_struct).unwrap();
let bincode_bytes = bincode::serialize(&my_struct).unwrap();
assert_eq!(wincode_bytes, bincode_bytes);
```

# pod_wrapper in solana_transaction::containers - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/solana-transaction/4.1.5/solana_transaction/containers/macro.pod_wrapper.html

```
macro_rules! pod_wrapper {
    ($(unsafe struct $name:ident($type:ty);)*) => { ... };
}
```
**crate feature**only.

`wincode`## Expand description

Creates a wrapper type for a type that is represented by raw bytes and does not have any invalid bit patterns.

By using `pod_wrapper!`, you are telling wincode that it can serialize and deserialize a type
with a single memcpy – it wont pay attention to things like struct layout, endianness, or
anything else that would require validity or bit pattern checks. This is a very strong claim to
make, so be sure that your type adheres to those requirements.

Composable with sequence [ containers](https://docs.rs/index.html) or compound types (structs, tuples) for
an optimized read/write implementation.

This can be useful outside of sequences as well, for example on newtype structs
containing byte arrays with `#[repr(transparent)]`.

💡 **Note:** as of `wincode` `0.2.0`, `pod_wrapper!` is no longer needed for types that wincode
can determine are “memcpy-safe”.

This includes:

- `u8`
- `[u8; N]`
- structs comprised of the above, and;
- annotated with `#[derive(SchemaWrite)]`or`#[derive(SchemaRead)]`, and;
- annotated with `#[repr(transparent)]`or`#[repr(C)]`.

- annotated with

Similarly, using built-in std collections like `Vec<T>` or `Box<[T]>` where `T` is one of the
above will also be automatically optimized.

You’ll really only need to reach for [ pod_wrapper!](https://docs.rs/macro.pod_wrapper.html) when dealing with foreign types for which
you cannot derive

`SchemaWrite` or `SchemaRead`. Or you’re in a controlled scenario where you
explicitly want to avoid endianness or layout checks.[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

- The type must allow any bit pattern (e.g., no `bool`s, no`char`s, etc.)
- If used on a compound type like a struct, all fields must be also be memcpy-able, its layout
must be guaranteed (via `#[repr(transparent)]`or`#[repr(C)]`), and the struct must not have any padding.
- Must not contain references or pointers (includes types like `Vec`or`Box`).- Note, you may use `pod_wrapper!`created types*inside*types like`Vec`or`Box`, e.g.,`Vec<PodT>`or`Box<[PodT]>`, but using`pod_wrapper!`on the outer type is invalid.

- Note, you may use

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

A repr-transparent newtype struct containing a byte array where you cannot derive `SchemaWrite`
or `SchemaRead`:

```
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Copy)]
#[repr(transparent)]
struct Address([u8; 32]);
wincode::pod_wrapper! {
    unsafe struct PodAddress(Address);
}
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, SchemaWrite, SchemaRead)]
struct MyStruct {
    #[wincode(with = "PodAddress")]
    address: Address
}
let my_struct = MyStruct {
    address: Address(array::from_fn(|i| i as u8)),
};
let wincode_bytes = wincode::serialize(&my_struct).unwrap();
let bincode_bytes = bincode::serialize(&my_struct).unwrap();
assert_eq!(wincode_bytes, bincode_bytes);
```

# AccountMeta in solana_transaction - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/solana-transaction/4.1.5/solana_transaction/struct.AccountMeta.html

```
#[repr(C)]pub struct AccountMeta {
    pub pubkey:
```
[Address](https://docs.rs/struct.Address.html),
    pub is_signer: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
    pub is_writable: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
}## Expand description

Describes a single account read or written by a program during instruction execution.

When constructing an [ Instruction](https://docs.rs/struct.Instruction.html), a list of all accounts that may be
read or written during the execution of that instruction must be supplied.
Any account that may be mutated by the program during execution, either its
data or metadata such as held lamports, must be writable.

Note that because the Solana runtime schedules parallel transaction
execution around which accounts are writable, care should be taken that only
accounts which actually may be mutated are specified as writable. As the
default [ AccountMeta::new](https://docs.rs/struct.AccountMeta.html#method.new) constructor creates writable accounts, this is
a minor hazard: use

[to specify that an account is not writable.](https://docs.rs/struct.AccountMeta.html#method.new_readonly)

`AccountMeta::new_readonly`## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.pubkey)

`pubkey: `[Address](https://docs.rs/struct.Address.html)An account’s public key.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.is_signer)

`is_signer: `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)True if an `Instruction` requires a `Transaction` signature matching `pubkey`.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.is_writable)

`is_writable: `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)True if the account data or metadata may be mutated during program execution.

```
let instr = Instruction::new_with_borsh(
    program_id,
    &instruction,
    vec![
        AccountMeta::new(from, true),
        AccountMeta::new(to, false),
        AccountMeta::new_readonly(from_account_storage, false),
    ],
);
```

# Address in solana_transaction - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/solana-transaction/4.1.5/solana_transaction/struct.Address.html

`pub struct Address(/* private fields */);`## Expand description

The address of a [Solana account](https://solana.com/docs/core/accounts).

Some account addresses are [ed25519](https://ed25519.cr.yp.to/) public keys, with corresponding secret
keys that are managed off-chain. Often, though, account addresses do not
have corresponding secret keys — as with [ program derived
addresses](https://solana.com/docs/core/cpi#program-derived-addresses) — or the secret key is not relevant to the operation
of a program, and may have even been disposed of. As running Solana programs
can not safely create or manage secret keys, the full

[is not defined in](https://docs.rs/solana-sdk/latest/solana_sdk/signer/keypair/struct.Keypair.html)

`Keypair``solana-program` but in `solana-sdk`.## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

**crate features**only.

`curve25519` or `syscalls`Checks whether the given address lies on the Ed25519 curve.

On-curve addresses correspond to valid Ed25519 public keys (and therefore can have associated private keys). Off-curve addresses are typically used for program-derived addresses (PDAs).

# CompiledInstruction in solana_transaction - Rust

pub struct CompiledInstruction {
    pub program_id_index:
```
[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html),
    pub accounts: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)>,
    pub data: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)>,
}## Expand description

A compact encoding of an instruction.

A `CompiledInstruction` is a component of a multi-instruction [ Message](https://docs.rs/struct.Message.html),
which is the core of a Solana transaction. It is created during the
construction of

`Message`. Most users will not interact with it directly.## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.program_id_index)

`program_id_index: `[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)Index into the transaction keys array indicating the program account that executes this instruction.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.accounts)

`accounts: `[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)>Ordered indices into the transaction keys array indicating which accounts to pass to the program.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.data)

`data: `[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)>The program input data.

# ShortU16 in solana_transaction - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/solana-transaction/4.1.5/solana_transaction/struct.ShortU16.html

`pub struct ShortU16(pub `[u16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u16.html));**crate feature**only.

`wincode`## Expand description

Same as u16, but serialized with 1 to 3 bytes. If the value is above 0x7f, the top bit is set and the remaining value is stored in the next bytes. Each byte follows the same pattern until the 3rd byte. The 3rd byte may only have the 2 least-significant bits set, otherwise the encoded value will overflow the u16.

## Tuple Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

use solana_short_vec::ShortU16;

# Signature in solana_transaction - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/solana-transaction/4.1.5/solana_transaction/struct.Signature.html

`pub struct Signature(/* private fields */);`## Expand description

A 64-byte Ed25519 signature.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/solana-signature/3.4.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/solana_signature/lib.rs.html#157)**crate features **`verify` only.

[Source](https://docs.rs/solana-signature/3.4.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/solana_signature/lib.rs.html#157)

**crate features**only.

`verify`Verifies this signature against `message_bytes` using `pubkey_bytes`.

`pubkey_bytes` is the signer’s Ed25519 public key, and `message_bytes`
is the exact message that was signed. Returns `false` if verification
fails or the public key cannot be parsed.

    BuiltinProgramsMustConsumeComputeUnits,
}## Expand description

Reasons the runtime might have rejected an instruction.

Members of this enum must not be removed, but new ones can be added. Also, it is crucial that meta-information if any that comes along with an error be consistent across software versions. For example, it is dangerous to include error strings from 3rd party crates because they could change at any time and changes to them are difficult to detect.

Allows on-chain programs to implement program-specific error types and see them returned by the Solana runtime. A program-specific error may be any type that is represented as or serialized to a u32 integer.

# TransactionError in solana_transaction - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/solana-transaction/4.1.5/solana_transaction/enum.TransactionError.html

```
pub enum TransactionError {
```
## Show 39 variants

    CommitCancelled,
}## Expand description

Reasons a transaction might be rejected.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.AccountInUse)

### AccountInUse

An account is already being processed in another transaction in a way that does not support parallelism

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.AccountLoadedTwice)

### AccountLoadedTwice

A `Pubkey` appears twice in the transaction’s `account_keys`.  Instructions can reference
`Pubkey`s more than once but the message must contain a list with no duplicate keys

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.AccountNotFound)

### AccountNotFound

Attempt to debit an account but found no record of a prior credit.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ProgramAccountNotFound)

### ProgramAccountNotFound

Attempt to load a program that does not exist

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.InsufficientFundsForFee)

### InsufficientFundsForFee

The from `Pubkey` does not have sufficient balance to pay the fee to schedule the transaction

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.InvalidAccountForFee)

### InvalidAccountForFee

This account may not be used to pay transaction fees

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.AlreadyProcessed)

### AlreadyProcessed

The bank has seen this transaction before. This can occur under normal operation
when a UDP packet is duplicated, as a user error from a client not updating
its `recent_blockhash`, or as a double-spend attack.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.BlockhashNotFound)

### BlockhashNotFound

The bank has not seen the given `recent_blockhash` or the transaction is too old and
the `recent_blockhash` has been discarded.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.InstructionError)

### InstructionError([u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html), [InstructionError](https://docs.rs/enum.InstructionError.html))

An error occurred while processing an instruction. The first element of the tuple indicates the instruction index in which the error occurred.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.CallChainTooDeep)

### CallChainTooDeep

Loader call chain is too deep

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.MissingSignatureForFee)

### MissingSignatureForFee

Transaction requires a fee but has no signature present

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.InvalidAccountIndex)

### InvalidAccountIndex

Transaction contains an invalid account reference

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.SignatureFailure)

### SignatureFailure

Transaction did not pass signature verification

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.InvalidProgramForExecution)

### InvalidProgramForExecution

This program may not be used for executing instructions

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.SanitizeFailure)

### SanitizeFailure

Transaction failed to sanitize accounts offsets correctly implies that account locks are not taken for this TX, and should not be unlocked.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ClusterMaintenance)

### ClusterMaintenance

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.AccountBorrowOutstanding)

### AccountBorrowOutstanding

Transaction processing left an account with an outstanding borrowed reference

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.WouldExceedMaxBlockCostLimit)

### WouldExceedMaxBlockCostLimit

Transaction would exceed max Block Cost Limit

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.UnsupportedVersion)

### UnsupportedVersion

Transaction version is unsupported

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.InvalidWritableAccount)

### InvalidWritableAccount

Transaction loads a writable account that cannot be written

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.WouldExceedMaxAccountCostLimit)

### WouldExceedMaxAccountCostLimit

Transaction would exceed max account limit within the block

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.WouldExceedAccountDataBlockLimit)

### WouldExceedAccountDataBlockLimit

Transaction would exceed account data limit within the block

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.TooManyAccountLocks)

### TooManyAccountLocks

Transaction locked too many accounts

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.AddressLookupTableNotFound)

### AddressLookupTableNotFound

Address lookup table not found

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.InvalidAddressLookupTableOwner)

### InvalidAddressLookupTableOwner

Attempted to lookup addresses from an account owned by the wrong program

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.InvalidAddressLookupTableData)

### InvalidAddressLookupTableData

Attempted to lookup addresses from an invalid account

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.InvalidAddressLookupTableIndex)

### InvalidAddressLookupTableIndex

Address table lookup uses an invalid index

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.InvalidRentPayingAccount)

### InvalidRentPayingAccount

Transaction leaves an account with a lower balance than rent-exempt minimum

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.WouldExceedMaxVoteCostLimit)

### WouldExceedMaxVoteCostLimit

Transaction would exceed max Vote Cost Limit

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.WouldExceedAccountDataTotalLimit)

### WouldExceedAccountDataTotalLimit

Transaction would exceed total account data limit

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.DuplicateInstruction)

### DuplicateInstruction([u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html))

Transaction contains a duplicate instruction that is not allowed

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.InsufficientFundsForRent)

### InsufficientFundsForRent

Transaction results in an account with insufficient funds for rent

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.MaxLoadedAccountsDataSizeExceeded)

### MaxLoadedAccountsDataSizeExceeded

Transaction exceeded max loaded accounts data size cap

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.InvalidLoadedAccountsDataSizeLimit)

### InvalidLoadedAccountsDataSizeLimit

LoadedAccountsDataSizeLimit set for transaction must be greater than 0.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ResanitizationNeeded)

### ResanitizationNeeded

Sanitized transaction differed before/after feature activation. Needs to be resanitized.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ProgramExecutionTemporarilyRestricted)

### ProgramExecutionTemporarilyRestricted

Program execution is temporarily restricted on an account.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.UnbalancedTransaction)

### UnbalancedTransaction

The total balance before the transaction does not equal the total balance after the transaction

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ProgramCacheHitMaxLimit)

### ProgramCacheHitMaxLimit

Program cache hit max limit.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.CommitCancelled)

### CommitCancelled

Commit cancelled internally.

# VersionedMessage in solana_transaction - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/solana-transaction/4.1.5/solana_transaction/enum.VersionedMessage.html

## Expand description

Either a legacy message, v0 or a v1 message.

[§](https://docs.rs#serialization)Serialization

If the first bit is set, the remaining 7 bits will be used to determine
which message version is serialized starting from version `0`. If the first
is bit is not set, all bytes are used to encode the legacy `Message`
format.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

`wincode`## Expand description

## Provided Associated Constants[§](https://docs.rs#provided-associated-consts)

Metadata about the type’s serialization.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety-1)Safety

It is always safe to leave this as the default `TypeMeta::Dynamic`. If
you set it to `TypeMeta::Static { size, zero_copy }`, you have to ensure
the following two points:

- `size`must always correspond to the number of bytes read by- `read`.
- If `zero_copy`is`true`,`Dst`’s in-memory representation must correspond exactly to the serialized form, and all byte sequences must be valid in-memory representations of`Dst`.

## Required Associated Types[§](https://docs.rs#required-associated-types)

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

[Source](https://docs.rs/wincode/0.5.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/wincode/schema/mod.rs.html#283)

[Source](https://docs.rs/wincode/0.5.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/wincode/schema/mod.rs.html#283)

Read into `dst` from `reader`.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety-2)Safety

You must initialize `dst` if **and only if** you return `Ok(())`. In the
`Err(…)` case, initializing `dst` can lead to memory leaks.

It is permissible to not initialize `dst` if `dst` is an inhabited
zero-sized type.

## Provided Methods[§](https://docs.rs#provided-methods)

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

### impl<'de, C> [SchemaRead](https://docs.rs/trait.SchemaRead.html)<'de, C> for [ShortU16](https://docs.rs/struct.ShortU16.html)

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use solana_short_vec::ShortU16;
let ShortU16(val) = wincode::deserialize(&[0x7f]).unwrap();
assert_eq!(val, 127);
```
```
use solana_short_vec::ShortU16;
let ShortU16(val) = wincode::deserialize(&[0x80, 0x01]).unwrap();
assert_eq!(val, 128);
```
```
use solana_short_vec::ShortU16;
let ShortU16(val) = wincode::deserialize(&[0x80, 0x80, 0x01]).unwrap();
assert_eq!(val, 16384);
```

`wincode`## Expand description

## Provided Associated Constants[§](https://docs.rs#provided-associated-consts)

Metadata about the type’s serialization.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety-1)Safety

It is always safe to leave this as the default `TypeMeta::Dynamic`. If
you set it to `TypeMeta::Static { size, zero_copy }`, you have to ensure
the following two points:

- `size`must always correspond to the number of bytes written by- `write`.- `size_of`must always return- `Ok(size)`.
- If `zero_copy`is`true`,`Src`’s in-memory representation must correspond exactly to the serialized form. There must be no padding in the in-memory representation of`Src`.

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*
